I fixed defect (2) in the feature-app skeleton, and all 8 acceptance commands pass.

What was wrong: in `list.html`, the `#record-table` container had `hx-boost="true"` and its own `hx-target`. Every link inside it inherited both, so clicking a record loaded the whole detail page into the list, giving two navigation bars.

What I changed:
- **`tables.py`**: new constant `UNBOOSTED_ROWS`. It turns the boost off on the table's rows and footer (`hx-boost="false"` on `<tbody>` and `<tfoot>`). `RecordTable` adds it to its `Meta.attrs`. Record links now load as normal pages. Sort links in the header and the paging links stay boosted, so they still refresh only the table.
- **`list.html`**: a template comment saying what the container boosts and where the rows turn it off.
- **`tests/test_views.py`**: a new test, `test_record_links_of_a_list_are_not_boosted`. It works out which `hx-boost` value applies to each link and checks that a list's record link is not boosted while its sort links are. Areas list every list and list panel in a new `LISTS` table.
- **`README.md`**: a new section, "HTMX boost on lists", says every area table must use `UNBOOSTED_ROWS`. Links inside other boosted containers, such as panels, need `hx-boost="false"` themselves. Every list and panel goes in `LISTS`. The file table mentions the new test.

To check it, I copied the skeleton into a throwaway copy of the app as area `sample`, set to Product. ruff, ruff format, djLint, `manage.py check`, makemigrations and all 21 tests passed on PostgreSQL and on SQL Server. With `UNBOOSTED_ROWS` removed, the new test fails as it should. I deleted the copy afterwards. The domain app is unchanged: 35 tests pass on both databases.

Items (3) to (6) are in other agents' paths, so they are in requests.
notes: The fix keeps hx-boost, hx-target and hx-swap on the #record-table container, so sort and paging links still refresh only the table. It turns the boost off on <tbody> and <tfoot> through the table's Meta.attrs (tables.UNBOOSTED_ROWS), using django-tables2's standard bootstrap5 template, so no custom table template is needed. Every link and form in a row now loads as a full page.

The new skeleton test works out which hx-boost value applies to each link with the standard-library html.parser, because htmx inherits the attribute from enclosing elements. It fails when a record link inherits a true boost, and also when the list has no sort link or its sort links are not boosted. I confirmed it fails on the old pattern.

I copied the skeleton into a throwaway copy of the app (area 'sample', Record = Product) and ran ruff, ruff format, djLint, manage.py check, makemigrations and 21 tests on PostgreSQL and SQL Server; all passed. I deleted the copy afterwards. Nothing in the target repo changed in this attempt.
